ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: With S2 closed and S1 open, what will the current waveform in the delta winding be?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the left side of the figure is a three-phase star/neutral-point-connected winding, with three terminals labeled A, B, C, and the other ends of the three-phase windings are connected to a common vertical bus; there is a neutral terminal N below, connected to this common point through switch S1, and S1 is in the open position in the figure. The right side is a three-phase delta-connected winding, with terminals labeled a, b, c; the lower switch S2 is located in the delta loop, and closing S2 will form a closed delta loop. Reasoning: the problem states that S2 is closed and S1 is open. When S1 is open, the neutral-line loop on the star side is unavailable, so zero-sequence/third-harmonic current cannot form an external loop through the neutral point on the star side. When S2 is closed, a closed loop is formed inside the delta winding. The third harmonic belongs to the triplen/zero-sequence components; they can circulate inside the closed delta winding, while the balanced fundamental wave will not appear as this kind of closed delta circulating current. Therefore, the current waveform in the delta winding contains only the third-harmonic component.
